item.title: MultiChoice welcomes NBC directive on content rights
item.description: MultiChoice Group has welcomed a directive by the National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) reaffirming regulations governing intellectual property rights and the retransmission of audiovisual content in Nigeria. The directive, issued on November 2, 2026, clarifies that access to another broadcasting operator’s signal does not automatically grant the right to retransmit or commercially redistribute its content. It further stipulates that operators must obtain the necessary rights and authorisations before retransmitting protected content, warning that unauthorised retransmission constitutes a violation of intellectual property rights. Welcoming the directive, Chief Executive Officer of MultiChoice Nigeria, Kemi Omotosho, described the NBC’s clarification as an important step towards protecting content creators and rights-holders and promoting a more orderly and sustainable broadcasting market. Omotosho said a clear and predictable regulatory framework would strengthen the creative ecosystem by encouraging investment in local content and creating long-term value for creators, rights-holders, operators and audiences. “The Group welcomes the NBC’s efforts to provide greater clarity on content rights and retransmission rules in Nigeria. This clarification is an important step towards strengthening the protection of creators and rights-holders and fostering a well-structured and sustainable audiovisual market. “A clear and predictable regulatory framework benefits the entire creative ecosystem, supporting investment in local content and creating long-term value for creators, rights-holders, operators and audiences alike,” she said. MultiChoice said the directive provides important regulatory guidance for the broadcasting industry, reinforcing the need to respect intellectual property rights, promote fair competition and ensure a level playing field for legitimate operators. It added that regulatory clarity was essential to encouraging investment in content creation, supporting the sustainability of the broadcasting industry and strengthening the relationship between creators, rights-holders, broadcasters and audiences. The Group reaffirmed its commitment to protecting intellectual property rights and supporting the sustainable development of Africa’s creative industries. It also pledged to continue working with regulators and industry stakeholders to promote legitimate content distribution and strengthen the long-term sustainability of the audiovisual sector. item.title: Subsidy is not coming back — Tinubu insists
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye President Bola Tinubu has ruled out restoring the fuel subsidy, saying his administration will instead expand support for farmers and invest in education, as he campaigned for re-election in Jigawa State. Tinubu spoke on Tuesday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Dutse Township Stadium, as part of the party’s nationwide campaign ahead of the 2027 general election. Addressing the subsidy debate, Tinubu said claims that fuel subsidy returns would return were false, arguing that public resources should be directed towards education and agriculture. “To those who say subsidy is coming back, it’s a lie. Don’t let them lie to you again. It’s not going to come back. We cannot spend the future of our children today and feel that they will grow tomorrow. No, they have to be in school. We have to invest in their education. We have to invest in agriculture,” he said. Tinubu said his administration would subsidise farming and reward small-scale farmers. He promised interest-free loans for farmers and said mechanised farming service centres would be established in six locations. “We will subsidise farming. We will reward small-scale farmers. Interest-free loans for farmers are coming. Prosperity is coming. Food security will happen. I hope you hear me, Jigawa. You hear me, Jigawa. There will be interest-free loans for small-scale farmers. We are going to install a mechanised farming service centre in six geographical locations: mechanised farming,” he said. He also said universities would play a greater role in agricultural research and development. “Our university will be more involved in research and development in agriculture than ever before,” Tinubu said. The president also addressed insecurity, saying his administration had strengthened the police and armed forces and was paying better salaries. “We will conquer insecurity. We’ve been through many wars; we will defeat our enemies, enemies of unity, enemies of stability, and enemies of hope. To assure you that we are doing that, we’ve strengthened the police, we’ve strengthened the armed forces, and we are paying better salaries today,” he added. item.title: NERC approves fresh N30bn for 11 DisCos to provide free meters
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved an additional N30 billion for the 11 electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) to procure and install free meters for unmetered customers, bringing total approvals under the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF) scheme to N79 billion. The latest approval, which represents the third tranche of the fund, is aimed at accelerating efforts to bridge Nigeria’s metering gap, reduce revenue losses and improve service delivery in the electricity distribution sector. The Commission had earlier approved N21 billion under Tranche A and N28 billion under Tranche B, bringing previous approvals to N49 billion. In Order No. NERC/2026/121, effective November 2, 2026, the regulator said the latest N30 billion would be allocated among the 11 DisCos in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund as of the July 2026 market settlement. According to the order, the funds would be used to meter all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerate the closure of the metering gap among customers classified under Band B. NERC specifically directed the DisCos to deploy the funds for the “procurement and installation of meters for unmetered Band ‘A’ and ‘B’ Customers within their franchise areas.” The intervention comes amid a national metering rate of 63.10 per cent as of August 2026, with 8.05 million of the 12.75 million active electricity customers having meters. Data from the Commission showed that approximately 4.7 million active customers were still without meters. Explaining the objectives of the MAF scheme, NERC said the fund was designed to accelerate meter deployment, close the existing metering gap, reduce commercial and collection losses for DisCos, enhance service quality and improve customer satisfaction. The regulator reiterated that all meters procured and installed under the scheme must be provided to customers free of charge. It stressed that “all meters procured and installed under the MAF framework shall be provided to customers at no cost.” The Commission also directed that every meter must prominently display the name of the relevant DisCo, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription, “NOT FOR SALE”. Under the order, the DisCos are required to conduct transparent procurement processes within 10 days to select eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stocks ready for deployment. They must also submit details of their selected providers and available meter inventories, including meter types, brands, serial numbers and locations, to the Commission within 15 days for a no-objection approval. NERC adopted the median national MAP online bid price from the September 2026 bidding cycle as the maximum procurement price for each meter category. item.title: Video: Noise, mob can’t determine who leads Nigeria – Segalink
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Human rights activist and social commentator, Segun Awosanya, popularly known as Segalink, has said that noise, mob pressure and ethnic sentiments should not determine who becomes Nigeria’s president. Awosanya made the remark during an interview on Vanguard’s Politics Hub, where he spoke about the quality of political candidates and the growing influence of public sentiment in determining political choices ahead of the 2027 general elections. He argued that several capable politicians had been relegated in the country’s political conversations, despite what he described as their leadership qualities and experience. Citing former Minister of Education, Adewole Adebayo, former presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, former Governor of Cross River State, Donald Duke, and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, among others, Awosanya said the country should pay greater attention to the qualities and capacity of its political candidates. “There are other people that we have totally relegated, like I said, that are quality candidates. We have the Adewole of the SDP, we have the Sowores of this world, we have the Donald Duke of this world, we have the Makindes. These are quality people who certain candidates cannot even lace their shoes,” he said. He maintained that political conversations should focus on what candidates intend to do differently for the country rather than the popularity they enjoy or the crowd they command. According to him, Nigerians should not allow what he described as ethnic agendas, mob sentiments and aggressive supporters to dictate the country’s leadership choices. “Let us not look at the noise, the mob, or the crowd, or the irate or virulent people who want to force their way into our hearts, or into our nation for their own ethnic agenda. They should not be the decider of who becomes the leader of this country. That’s what we’re saying,” he added. The activist also criticised the use of insults and the denigration of political opponents as strategies for gaining political power, arguing that such behaviour was not a substitute for presenting credible alternatives to Nigerians. “I’ve never seen in any country where people insult their way to power, where people believe that by denigrating other people, by bending other people’s work to disrepute, will make them preferred,” he said. Awosanya called for more honest conversations about the country’s political choices, insisting that Nigerians should be willing to confront uncomfortable realities rather than excuse conduct that undermines constructive political engagement. item.title: $500m loan: Don’t saddle your successor with debt, Atiku tells Tinubu
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has warned President Bola Tinubu against committing Nigeria to a proposed $500 million World Bank loan shortly before the end of his current four-year tenure, arguing that no administration should saddle the country with fresh debt without adequate justification and public scrutiny. Atiku said the proposed borrowing, scheduled for consideration a few days before the May 29, 2027 presidential inauguration, could constrain the next administration and impose repayment obligations on Nigerians without giving them an opportunity to scrutinise the decision. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku described the proposed loan as an attempt to mortgage Nigeria’s future and urged the World Bank not to approve the facility on the contemplated timetable. “Taking loans as if you were a drunken sailor is a road to economic bondage, a second slavery. If this government is determined to mortgage Nigeria’s future and place our country at the mercy of creditors, we will not accept it,” he said. Atiku expressed concern over the timing of the proposed facility, which, according to the report he cited, is scheduled for consideration on May 25, 2027, barely four days before the next presidential inauguration. He accused the Tinubu administration of attempting to commit the country to fresh financial obligations in the closing days of its current tenure, warning that such a decision could complicate governance for the incoming administration. “The Tinubu administration’s latest move is a preemptive attempt to lock Nigeria into a path of economic instability, even after Nigerians have roundly rejected its poverty-inflicting reforms. A government cannot use its final days in office to bind the country and make governance more difficult for its successor,” he said. Invoking a Swahili proverb, the former Vice-President warned that borrowing shortly before the end of a presidential tenure could leave a successor constrained by obligations imposed by creditors. “As the Swahili proverb warns, ‘If you borrow a man’s legs, you will go where he directs.’ A leader who borrows on his way out leaves his successor walking on the lender’s legs, constrained by obligations and choices the people did not make,” Atiku said. He called on the World Bank to defer consideration of the proposed facility, insisting that Nigerians must first be allowed to scrutinise its terms, risks and repayment obligations. “We call on the World Bank not to approve this proposed loan on the timetable now being contemplated. Nigerians deserve full disclosure of its terms, risks and repayment obligations, and the opportunity to scrutinise a commitment that will outlast the administration pursuing it,” he said. item.title: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being ‘cowards’
item.description: At least 66 soldiers in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) have been sentenced to death for cowardice, mutiny and disobeying orders following a military trial in the country’s conflict-hit eastern region, local media have reported. The soldiers were among 71 military personnel tried before a military court in Walikale, North Kivu province. Four were acquitted, while another received a 10-year prison sentence. The Congolese army said the trial was aimed at strengthening discipline among troops fighting armed groups in the east, where years of insecurity have continued to undermine government control. The soldiers were reportedly arrested on October 20 in Walikale after allegedly abandoning their positions and fleeing during clashes with fighters from the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), a rebel coalition that includes the M23 group. The army’s operations against armed groups, particularly the M23, have repeatedly been affected by poor discipline and disorganisation within its ranks. The government has consistently accused neighbouring Rwanda of backing the M23, an allegation denied by Kigali and the rebels, despite what has been described as overwhelming evidence. The Congolese military has also faced criticism over its professionalism, while soldiers have complained about poor salaries and inadequate equipment. Last month, another 27 soldiers were sentenced to death on similar charges of cowardice after reportedly withdrawing from frontline positions during clashes with rebels. DR Congo reinstated the death penalty in March 2024 after lifting a moratorium that had been in place for 20 years. The government said the decision was necessary to eliminate “traitors” within the military. Authorities also said capital punishment would apply to individuals involved in armed groups, insurrection, treason and war crimes. The move attracted widespread criticism from human rights organisations. However, no formal executions have been carried out since the death penalty was reinstated. Since the beginning of 2025, at least 507 soldiers have been convicted, including 381 death sentences, according to figures compiled by French broadcaster RFI. In October 2025, former Congolese President Joseph Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia over charges including war crimes and treason. Kabila denied the allegations but did not appear in court to defend himself. He has since been named as the leader of the FRN. item.title: We’ll provide reliable power in Nigeria – Tinubu
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab President Bola Tinubu has promised to provide reliable electricity, create more job opportunities and reduce the cost of living as part of efforts to improve the country’s economy. Tinubu made the pledge on Tuesday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital. He said his administration would pursue a stronger industrial base, support nano, micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and expand employment opportunities for Nigerians. “We will lower the cost of living. We will provide reliable power, not the whole privatisation that is not working. We will provide you with reliable power in this Nigeria,” he said. On economic reforms, Tinubu said his administration would continue with the removal of petrol subsidy and sustain programmes such as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). He further pledged that money recovered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) from financial irregularities would be channelled into NELFUND to support students seeking access to higher education. Vanguard reported that Tinubu at the event also promised to establish six mechanised farming service centres across the country’s six geopolitical zones, alongside increased investment in irrigation and agricultural research, to boost food production and reduce prices. item.title: ‘It’s a farce’, US defense secretary Hegseth rejects impeachment push
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday denounced a push to impeach him as a “farce” and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under President Donald Trump. “It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the impeachment push “slander” and “sabotage.” Hegseth’s combative performance came as Congress inched toward a rare vote on impeachment over alleged misconduct related to wars against Iran and Yemen’s Houthis, and the controversial killing of alleged drug smugglers in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. The effort throws down a challenge to Trump, already weakened by last week’s midterms drubbing, where anger at the sputtering Iran war and subsequent surge in fuel prices helped drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans. Trump has acknowledged that the Iran war contributed to his party losing both the House and Senate in Congress. But moments after Hegseth’s televised press conference, the 80-year-old president signaled his backing. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. The expected vote in the House comes in the lame duck period when Republicans still retain their narrow majority, ahead of next January when the huge new Democratic majority takes over. If a majority in the House voted in favor, the Senate would still need a two thirds majority to convict and remove Hegseth — a tall order even after Democrats take up power there too in January. The impeachment articles have been introduced by a Republican Trump critic, Thomas Massie, who will exit Congress after losing his seat. Trump called Massie “a disgruntled, angry, defeated former Congressman” and “a TOTAL LOSER!” – ‘Would do it again’ – Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers. “I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said, also seeking to equate the effort to remove him with an attack on US troops. “These resolutions tell every one of them that their service was a crime. Their service was not a crime. These are heroes,” said Hegseth. Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions. Hegseth has called the widely unpopular war a “courageous and historic effort.” The 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis also features in Massie’s articles of impeachment, which charge Hegseth with starting the operation without congressional approval and in the absence of an imminent threat to the United States. item.title: Amaechi Accuses APC Of Dodging Policy Debate, Focusing On Opposition
item.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of concentrating on opposition figures rather than presenting its policies and plans to Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State and minister of transportation, said the ruling party was more interested in weakening the opposition than engaging Nigerians on critical national issues. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Tuesday. According to him, the APC’s campaign rallies have largely focused on attacking opposition figures, particularly him, rather than addressing issues affecting the country. “The party in power is trying to look for how to weaken the opposition; they are scared. Don’t you see their campaign? Tell me one state they have campaigned in that is not about Amaechi; it’s all Amaechi, Amaechi, Amaechi, Ebonyi, Rivers, Amaechi,” he said. ﻿ Policy Debate Amaechi contrasted the ruling party’s approach with the opposition’s campaign, saying his party had focused on issues such as the economy, social housing and security. “When we were campaigning, we were addressing issues. We addressed the issues of economy, social housing, security,” the ex-minister said. Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026. He further argued that the APC was using his name as a recurring subject at its campaign events instead of explaining what it intended to do if re-elected. “You know what I do every morning? I call my children, [and] I say, ‘You see, your father has achieved so much that he is now the issue in the political discourse of Nigeria.’ NDC is not calling my name because we are in opposition. Anywhere APC is going tomorrow, it’s Amaechi they will mention; they won’t mention what they will do,” he said. View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. The former governor also dismissed what he described as the ruling party’s assurances that things would improve in the future, arguing that Nigerians deserved concrete policy proposals rather than promises. “They are not interested; what they are interested in is, ‘don’t worry, things will be better in the future, just put us in power.’ It’s a referendum,” he added. Amaechi contested the ADC presidential primary ahead of the 2027 election but lost to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is currently Atiku’s running mate on the party’s ticket. item.title: Actor Olumide Oworu to contest for Reps after 2023 ballot exclusion
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nollywood actor and politician, Olumide Oworu has announced his intention to contest for a seat in the House of Representatives in the 2027 general elections. Oworu is seeking to represent Surulere I Federal Constituency of Lagos State under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), following his unsuccessful attempt to contest for the Lagos State House of Assembly in 2023. The actor made the announcement in a statement shared on his Instagram page on Tuesday, where he reflected on his previous political experience and expressed renewed determination to serve his community. View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Fresh Prince of Lagos (@olumideoworu) Recalling his 2023 political journey, Oworu said administrative challenges prevented his name from appearing on the final ballot despite his efforts to participate in the election. He described the experience as a learning process rather than a reason to abandon his political ambition. “Despite the administrative hurdles that left our names off the final ballot, your resilience showed me that our vision was never a passing phase. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he stated. “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices. If we don’t step up now, we will remain at the receiving end of broken systems tomorrow.” Declaring his latest ambition, the actor said he was proud to contest for the House of Representatives seat in the 2027 elections under the APM. “That is why I am incredibly proud to declare my candidacy for the House of Representatives (Surulere 1 Federal Constituency) in the 2027 elections under the banner of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).” In 2023, Oworu contested for the Surulere Constituency I seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party, where he was expected to challenge incumbent lawmaker Desmond Elliot. However, his name was missing from the final ballot, with Adebayo Bode listed as the Labour Party candidate. item.title: Nigerians miss Buhari; life was better under him — Amaechi
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Minister of Transportation and Vice Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi has said Nigerians are missing former President Muhammadu Buhari because, in his assessment, life was better under the late president than under the current APC-led administration. Speaking on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Tuesday, Amaechi challenged Nigerians to compare their lives under the two administrations as he made the case against President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. He cited the exchange rate, fuel prices and alleged corruption, and urged Nigerians to compare their lives under Buhari with their circumstances today. “I always like to quote the former president, Buhari. He will say, ‘People will call me back.’ Nigerians will say, ‘We miss former President Buhari’; are they not saying that now?” Amaechi said. “The reason why they are saying that is: compare your life when President Buhari was alive and was the president of Nigeria, and your life now; which one will you choose?” He said the dollar was about ₦600 and fuel cost less than ₦300 by the time the Buhari administration left office and also argued that allegations of stealing under Buhari did not compare with what he said was happening under the current government. “By the time we left office, dollar was at 600, by the time we left office, fuel was below 300, the stealing in Buhari’s government, if there was stealing in Buhari’s government, can you compare it to what is going on now?” he said. “What is going on now is what I call ‘Alibaba and the 40 thieves’.” Amaechi further alleged that contractors in the Ministry of Transportation had been arrested as authorities looked for evidence of wrongdoing during his time as minister. “They have arrested almost all the contractors in the Ministry of transport, looking for what I have done in the ministry,” he added. Addressing the coastal road project, Amaechi said: “The president chose to construct the coastal road because of the benefits he will get.” When asked whether some of the problems the Tinubu administration is trying to resolve stemmed from decisions taken under Buhari, citing Buhari’s refusal to remove fuel subsidy as an example, Amaechi authoritatively dismissed the claims. “Name one,” Amaechi replied. Amaechi also defended the ADC’s plan to reintroduce fuel subsidy if elected, saying the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, had proposed a system tied to domestic production. He said the ADC believed Buhari was right not to remove the subsidy, even though Amaechi himself had been among those who urged the former president to do so at the time. “We (the ADC) have said we will re-introduce fuel subsidy because the fuel subsidy he removed was wrong, Buhari refused to remove fuel subsidy because he told us clearly. item.title: Tinubu seeks Senate confirmation of NMDPRA executive directors, board secretary
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged the Senate to confirm the appointments of Executive Directors and Secretary of the Board of Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). Tinubu’s request is contained in a letter addressed to the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and read at plenary on Tuesday. Tinubu, in the letter, said the appointments were made in accordance with the provisions of Section 41, Subsections 2 and 3 of Petroleum Industry Act, 2021. He listed the nominees for reappointment to include Mr Abiodun Adeniji, Executive Director, Finance and Accounts and Mr Ogbugo Ukoha, Executive Director, Distribution Systems, Storage and Retailing Infrastructure. Dr Mustapha Lamode, the Executive Director, Health, Safety, Environment and Community, was also listed for reappointment. Tinubu also listed the nominees for new appointments to include Mr Mobolaji Musa as Executive Director, Hydrocarbon Processing Plants, Installation and Partnership and Ms Ogechukwu Modie as Executive Director, Economic Regulation and Strategic Planning. Others are Mr Said Abutali as Executive Director, Corporate Services and Administration, and Mrs Jumoke Gafar as Board Secretary and Legal Adviser. The President expressed the hope that the senate would consider and confirm the nominees in its usual expeditious manner. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Akpabio, thereafter, referred the letter to the Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas) for further legislative inputs and to revert to plenary within one week. item.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation Of Up To $1.4 Trillion
item.description: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, putting the company’s total valuation at up to $1.4 trillion. The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of “between $70.00 and $78.00” per share, amounting to $64.3 billion. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16. This photograph shows the logo of the US artificial intelligence safety and research company Anthropic displayed on a smartphone’s screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP On Monday, the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. On Tuesday, the company said its annualized projection, known as the run-rate revenue, “was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.” Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic’s valuation at up to a staggering $2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street. Several US media outlets, including The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times on Tuesday estimated the valuation of the company at between $1.3 trillion and $1.4 trillion. item.title: 2027: Duke seeks opposition unity as PRP unveils manifesto
item.description: Presidential candidate of People’s Redemption Party (PRP), Mr Donald Duke, on Tuesday in Abuja unveiled his ‘A Compact for Nigeria’s Renewal’ manifesto. Duke, at the occasion, urged opposition parties to bridge their differences, not for personal ambition, but to safeguard the nation’s democratic foundations. He warned that repeating what he called the miscalculations of the 2023 elections in 2027 would bring ‘lasting shame’. “We erred in 2023, and we are repeating the same in 2027. It is said, Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. The shame will certainly be on us,” he remarked. Duke called for an unconventional tactical thinking among opposition forces to counter what he termed an ‘unguarded political establishment’. “David did not defeat Goliath in a wrestling bout, but by strategy and unconventional means,” he stated. While building on the party’s strategic outlook, PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, said the occasion served as a vital vehicle to transition the party from mere aspirations to governing reality. Baba-Ahmed praised the party’s presidential candidate and his running mate, Malam Sule Mohammed, alongside more than 500 other candidates. He described them as models of integrity, competence and courage designed to lead the nation out of its current economic and security quagmire. The national chairman acknowledged the immense challenges that plagued the party, including competing against incumbent politicians who relied on state power and immense financial resources. “We will find resistance from politicians who bribe our people for our future, while we ask for trust and the courage to choose quality and integrity,” he said. He also urged supporters to reject vote-buying, declaring, “Nigeria and Nigerians are not for sale. item.title: 2027: Study our manifesto, judge us by promises kept – Presidency tells Nigerians
item.description: …As APC-PCC unveils 4-point manifesto, 8 priority areas By Soni Daniel (Editor, North), Emma Ujah (Bureau Chief, Abuja) & Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA The Presidency has urged Nigerians to study the past and current manifestoes of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC and judge the party by the promises it has kept since 2023, when it assumed power. The Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, gave the charge on Tuesday in Abuja at the unveiling of the APC manifesto, titled ‘From Reforms to Prosperity’. He described the manifesto as a binding pact with the electorate. “A manifesto, in its strictest sense, is simply a contract between the people and their leaders. It is an inviolable contract, and we take the strict interpretation of what a manifesto represents as gospel under this administration,” he said. He admitted that the reforms had put real pressure on households, adding that the people living through it deserve to be heard. “Nobody should have to pretend that life is easy at the moment,” he said. The former House Speaker nonetheless defended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to act, saying Tinubu confronted the subsidy burden and a distorted foreign exchange system when he took responsibility for the country in 2023. “Leaving those problems untouched would have continued to weaken our ability to invest in the future. The difference between a politician and a leader is that while a politician thinks about the next election, a leader thinks about the next generation. And that is exactly what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated,” Gbajabiamila said. 4 pillars The manifesto rests on four pillars: a secure and resilient nation; a better quality and more affordable life for every Nigerian; energy, infrastructure and economic growth; and effective and accountable governance. They are tied to the eight priority areas of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which the document says will be carried out on four foundations: macroeconomic stability, the rule of law, institutional capability and national cohesion. By 2031, the document commits to power generation scaled towards 10,000 megawatts, annual economic growth of 6 per cent, and youth unemployment and out-of-school children both halved. It also promises 20,000 additional teachers and health insurance expanded from more than 23 million enrollees to 40 per cent of Nigerians. item.title: Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO
item.description: Cholera has killed more than 3,000 people worldwide since the start of the year, the World Health Organization said Tuesday, insisting its goal of cutting global cases by 90 percent by 2030 remained in reach. The disease killed nearly 7,900 people in 2025, making it “the deadliest year for cholera since 1999”, according to Lorenzo Pezzoli, WHO lead for epidemic-prone bacterial diseases. While data for the first nine months of 2026 show a decline in deaths, more than 3,000 people have still died from the preventable and treatable diarrheal infection, he said, with “nearly nine out of 10 of them in Africa”. The WHO also warned that the current El Nino weather pattern could worsen outbreaks, as cholera can be fuelled by both flooding and water shortages. The UN health agency and the vaccine alliance, Gavi, aim to reduce global cholera cases by 90 percent by 2030 through mass vaccination campaigns and improved access to clean water and sanitation. Although cholera was eliminated from high-income countries generations ago thanks to safe drinking water and modern sewage systems, it can still “kill within a matter of hours” if left untreated, Pezzoli said, despite being “easy and inexpensive to treat” with existing medicines. “The 2030 goal is achievable because the work is already under way,” Pezzoli added, pointing to the International Coordinating Group (ICG) on Vaccine Provision, which last year approved the supply of 71 million doses, funded by Gavi. Vaccines and rapid diagnostic tests are also reaching outbreak zones more quickly, helping health workers detect and respond to infections earlier. WHO and its partners are helping countries identify districts where cholera repeatedly resurfaces and develop response plans. Seven countries — Angola, Bangladesh, the DR Congo, Nigeria, South Sudan, Sudan and Yemen — accounted for about 90 percent of global cases and deaths last year. “The collective response is undeniably bearing fruit, but… it remains insufficient,” Pezzoli said. “We must redouble our efforts to help all these countries reach the elimination goal which means ensuring that, by 2030, cholera no longer poses a public health threat in any of them.” The post Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate donates N100m to Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, Flamingos

Abdul Ningi (ADC-Bauchi Central) on the need to congratulate the victorious girls on their achievement. Ningi described the victory as historic, noting that the young players had achieved what several other Nigerian national teams had struggled to accomplish. item.title: Video: Tinubu can win votes without visiting all 36 states – Segalink
item.description: Human rights activist and social commentator, Segun Awosanya, popularly known as Segalink, has said President Bola Tinubu does not need to physically visit all 36 states of the federation to campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Awosanya argued that the President could adopt alternative means of reaching voters, including televised addresses and mobilisation through his campaign council, rather than relying solely on physical campaign visits. He made the remarks during an interview on Vanguard’s Politics Hub while discussing the president’s campaign strategy and the need to communicate directly with Nigerians ahead of the next general election. According to him, there is no rule requiring a presidential candidate to visit every state before an election, provided other effective mechanisms are deployed to communicate the candidate’s message and mobilise support. “It is not left for him to say 12 states is enough for me, while I can now adopt other mechanisms. There are so many things the President does that he doesn’t do directly,” he said. Awosanya explained that Tinubu could delegate grassroots mobilisation and campaign activities to his campaign council while personally engaging Nigerians through other communication channels. He likened the approach to the evolution of communication methods, arguing that people should not be restricted to outdated procedures when more convenient alternatives are available. “Just like when they write a rule that you must use a donkey to transfer one document from point A to point B. This time around, we don’t use donkeys any longer. Will you say if I mail it, if I email it, or if I send it as a WhatsApp message attachment or so, have I not communicated? So that’s the same thing,” he added. The activist further argued that presidential campaigns should be judged by their ability to connect with voters and communicate policy messages rather than the number of states a candidate physically visits. He said the objective should be to reach the people, win their confidence and secure support in states considered critical to the candidate’s electoral chances. “It’s not just about the performative optics; if he has gone to all the states. It’s about reaching the people there, it’s about getting his message across to the people. “It’s about ensuring that he wins hearts and minds in those states, and those ones that are critical to his winning the elections,” Awosanya said. He maintained that a presidential candidate could combine physical appearances with delegated campaign activities and televised engagements to reach a wider audience without personally travelling across the country. item.title: Why an Instagram Following Tracker Can Reveal More Than a Profile’s Follower Count
item.description: A popular Instagram account can attract thousands of followers, but that number rarely tells the whole story. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time. An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics. They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry. The Following list offers a different perspective. Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating. Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category. Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest. Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further. The Difference Between Following and Followers Before using an Instagram following tracker, it’s important to distinguish two commonly confused terms. Followers are people who subscribe to an account’s updates. Following refers to the accounts that the profile has chosen to follow. For example, a creator may have 40,000 followers while following only 600 accounts. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator. Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added. The order in which accounts appear should not be treated as a reliable record of recent follows. To understand changes, the list needs to be observed across different periods. item.title: What an Instagram Likes Viewer Can Tell Us About the Content People Enjoy
item.description: People reveal different sides of themselves on Instagram. Their profiles may feature carefully selected photographs, polished videos, and short biographies, but their everyday interactions with content can tell another story. A person who rarely posts about travel may regularly like photographs of unfamiliar destinations. A creator known for fashion might engage with technology tutorials, food videos, or sports content. These interactions can suggest topics that attract someone’s attention, even when they don’t appear on the person’s own profile. An Instagram likes viewer can help organize detected likes from public accounts, making it easier to identify recurring content themes rather than examining isolated posts. However, likes are an imperfect signal. They may indicate enjoyment, curiosity, support, or simply a momentary reaction. Understanding their limitations is essential before drawing conclusions. Why Instagram Likes Are So Interesting A like is one of the simplest interactions on social media. It takes only a moment, but it can reflect many different motivations. Someone might like a photograph because they admire the subject, appreciate the photography, support a friend, or agree with a message. For content creators and marketers, likes also form part of the wider picture of audience engagement. A beauty influencer may notice that certain makeup tutorials attract more engagement than product announcements. A restaurant could discover that behind-the-scenes videos generate stronger reactions than ordinary menu photographs. These observations can guide content decisions, especially when combined with comments, shares, reach, and other performance metrics. But there is an important difference between analyzing engagement on your own posts and studying what a particular public account likes elsewhere. Instagram makes the first task relatively straightforward. The second is more complicated. Can You See What Someone Likes on Instagram? Instagram lets users inspect the likes associated with individual posts they can access. For example, if a public photograph has received likes, its visible engagement information may show which accounts interacted with it. What Instagram doesn’t provide is a single public page listing all the posts another person has liked. The platform removed its old Following Activity tab in 2019. That feature previously offered a window into some activities of accounts people followed. Today, users can still explore publicly visible interactions, but building a comprehensive history of another account’s likes is not a standard Instagram feature. This is why an Instagram likes viewer is different from simply opening a photograph and checking its engagement. A viewer attempts to gather detectable likes associated with a selected account and present them together across reporting periods. What Can Repeated Likes Suggest?
